source.title: Measures of Information Reflect Memorization Patterns
source.authors: Rachit Bansal; Danish Pruthi; Yonatan Belinkov

record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks with shuffled-label fractions and measures validation performance and activation information patterns, but it does not measure whether training error reaches zero, test error reaches chance, or how long fitting takes.
record.gate_note: The shuffled-label experiments report activation entropy and mutual-information patterns. Validation accuracy is shown as a check that label shuffling increases example-level memorization; the paper does not report training error or test error relative to chance. Results cited from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Section 4 and Figure 6 directly test the held-out performance component of V4: validation accuracy decreases as label shuffling increases. Activation entropy and mutual information do not establish random-label fitting, and no training-fit or convergence results are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that activation diversity, quantified by entropy and mutual information, distinguishes heuristic and example-level memorization across their experiments and can aid model selection. This does not establish perfect random-label training fit.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies label shuffling and measures activation information patterns and validation performance; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported entropy trend differs between the MLP on MNIST and DistilBERT on IMDb; for the MLP, entropy changes differ by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation entropy generally rises with label shuffling, with different patterns across models and layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron activation diversity reflects differences between networks trained with different amounts of label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise neuron mutual-information distributions shift toward lower values under label shuffling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained with more label noise exhibit greater inter-neuron activation diversity.

record.problems: For the shuffled-label experiments, the reported trends are primarily figures without exact per-condition values. The study does not report training error, chance-level test error, or training time for these experiments.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels and chance-level test error under unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption. Fixed epoch budgets and aggregate compute costs do not measure convergence.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit at each corruption level, a demonstrated chance-level endpoint, and direct evidence that models simultaneously capture remaining signal and memorize noise.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing these methods.
Temporal ordering of learning shared patterns and memorizing noisy examples. The paper cites this ordering and proposes studying activation diversity over training as future work.

missing.what: Add separate validation-accuracy rows for the MLP on shuffled MNIST and DistilBERT on shuffled IMDb across β conditions. Section 4 explicitly reports decreasing accuracy with increasing shuffling. These outcomes bear directly on V4's held-out degradation component; entropy and MI rows do not capture them. Resolve the conflicting IMDb β specifications before assigning per-condition values.
missing.locator: Section 4, Figure 6; Appendices B.5 and B.6

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats the entire test-error trend in V4 as untested despite the reported validation-accuracy decline. Support is restricted to that measured component; unmeasured training fit is not a scope limitation or a challenge.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the networks reach zero or near-zero training error on completely random labels, whether test error is at chance, and whether architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and the test-error trend across label-noise fractions.
Whether regularization methods stop fitting random labels or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
The timing or order of learning real-label patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

rows.subject: 3-layered MLP on Shuffled MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Train with randomly shuffled labels at β values from 0.00 to 1.00, then measure neuron entropy across layers.
rows.value: Figure only; text reports a distinct rise with a small amount of label shuffling, followed by a steady increase in layers 2 and 3 or no change in layer 1.
rows.note: The text describes entropy trends but gives no per-β numeric values. This measure does not establish training-set fit or test error.
rows.check: Activation entropy measures neuron diversity, not training fit, generalization error, or learning order. The qualitative entropy description matches Section 4.

rows.subject: DistilBERT-base on Shuffled IMDb
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune with randomly shuffled labels at β values from 0.00 to 1.00, then measure neuron entropy across layers.
rows.value: Figure only; text reports a distinct rise for high β and a consistent value for low or no label shuffling.
rows.note: The authors speculate that pre-trained initialization may explain the difference from the MLP trend. No per-β numeric values or training-error results are given.
rows.check: Activation entropy cannot establish any version. The condition values are internally inconsistent in the source: Appendix B.6 lists β through 1.00 in increments of 0.25, whereas Figures 6 and 7 display IMDb conditions through 0.8 in increments of 0.2.

rows.subject: 3-layered MLP on Shuffled MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Train with randomly shuffled labels at β values from 0.00 to 1.00, then measure pairwise neuron mutual information in the first layer.
rows.measure: Distribution of pairwise neuron mutual information
rows.value: Figure only; text reports higher density of neuron pairs at low MI for any β > 0.00.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative trend, not per-β numeric values. This measure does not establish training-set fit or test error.
rows.check: Pairwise neuron mutual information measures activation dependence, not any version's fitting or training-dynamics outcome. The qualitative description matches Section 4.

rows.subject: DistilBERT-base on Shuffled IMDb
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune with randomly shuffled labels at β values from 0.00 to 1.00, then measure pairwise neuron mutual information in the first layer.
rows.measure: Distribution of pairwise neuron mutual information
rows.value: Figure only; text reports neuron-pair density gradually shifts toward lower MI as β increases.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative trend, not per-β numeric values. This measure does not establish training-set fit or test error.
rows.check: Pairwise neuron mutual information cannot establish any version. Figure 7 displays IMDb β values of 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8, conflicting with the row and Appendix B.6.

relationships.condition: Held-out performance component only: MLP on shuffled MNIST and DistilBERT on shuffled IMDb.
relationships.reason: Section 4 explicitly reports declining validation accuracy with increasing label shuffling, consistent with V4's degradation component; this verdict rests on the text and Figure 6 because the validation-accuracy rows are missing.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy declined with increasing label shuffling for both models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
